reason: The text demonstrates Yahweh's care for His people through multiple explicit actions: (1) He distinguishes the Israelites from Egyptians, protecting them from the plague while striking Egypt's firstborn—'to all the children of Israel not a dog shall bark' (וּלְכֹ֣ל בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל לֹ֤א יֶֽחֱרַץ־ כֶּ֙לֶב֙); (2) He grants the Israelites favor in Egyptian eyes ('the Lord gave the people favor in the sight of the Egyptians') enabling them to claim silver and gold; (3) He takes direct action to release them from bondage ('After this he will send you out from here'); (4) He provides specific instructions through Moses for their safe departure. These actions collectively demonstrate active, protective, and liberative care for the Israelite people.
